title: Run-bar decompression reveal
question: In each cyan lane, read the bars from left to right. A dark bar means black cells and a pale bar means white cells; the bar height in small grid steps is that run's length. Expand the runs into one row per lane, then stack the lanes from top to bottom. Which symbol appears: zigzag, key, anchor, or bell?

task_signature.mechanism: Locate ten visibly framed lanes, translate each left-to-right sequence of colored bar heights into alternating-valued run lengths, expand each sequence to a binary row, stack the rows, and classify the recovered glyph.

latent_z.description: The rendered scene contains the complete run tokens plus answer-independent palette, translation, and canvas nuisances.

latent_alias.justification: Every encoded run, token translation, palette choice, and canvas extent changes visible pixels; the decoded decision is computed only from the visibly rendered encoded runs, so no render-invariant latent relabeling is declared.

boundary.observable: The decision boundary is the visible integer bar-height lattice: changing a bar by one grid step changes one decoded run length, and the reported margin is the top-two Hamming-template score gap after decompression.
boundary.quarantine: Scenes with a top-two template gap below 12 decoded cells are quarantined as visually unstable.

semantic_contrast.contrast: Unlike opening-filter reveal, the transform uses no spatial neighborhood, erosion, dilation, or same-size cellular mask: it converts each bar's measured magnitude into a variable multiplicity of output cells. Unlike ranked-strip reassembly, no visible item is sorted or spatially permuted; bar magnitude is interpreted as a run length. Unlike equal-cell normalization or row zipping, the output has a different representational arity from the input tokens and requires value-to-multiplicity decompression in every lane.
semantic_contrast.expected_information_gain: This isolates whether a model can bind color to bit value, quantize visible bar height, and execute run-length decompression before recognizing a global symbol.
